text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me?
B: Yes. Hi.
A: I'm Tomasz.
B: Claire.
A: Ah. My wife is Claire.
B: Right. Everyone's been saying that sort of thing today. I had someone whose son's my son's age, same year and everything.
A: Yeah. Is a strange group.
B: Mm.
A: So, er, what do you do?
B: Midday supervisor at a primary school. You?
A: Kitchen fitter. Carpenter. In Basingstoke.
B: Our kitchen could do with you, honestly. It's the original one from when we bought the house, and none of the drawers shut properly.
A: Is it old house?
B: Nineteen-thirties semi. Nothing's square.
A: Yeah, the thirties houses, the walls go like this. You never get a straight line. But is okay, you scribe the worktop to the wall, you take your time. Is not a problem, is just slow. The problem is when the customer wants it finished in one day.
B: The showrooms make it sound like it's all going to be done in an afternoon. Everything's "seamless" and "your dream space."
A: Ha. Yeah. Dream space. Then I come and take the old one out and there is water under the sink from ten years.
B: That sounds more like it.
A: I had one lady, she changed the worktop colour three times. Already ordered. Three times.
B: Did you say anything?
A: No. I say okay. Is her kitchen.
B: You're more patient than me, then. I'd have said something.
A: Ha. Maybe. Er, what else you want to know?
B: I don't know. Where's your accent from? Sorry, if that's a rude question.
A: No, is fine. Poland. South-east, near Rzeszów. I've been here eighteen years.
B: I've been reading a Polish writer, actually. Olga Tokarczuk. Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead. Do you know it?
A: I know the name, she won the big prize, yeah? Nobel. My mum was talking about it. But I didn't read it. I'm not big reader, to be honest.
B: It's very odd. An old woman in a village near the Czech border who's obsessed with astrology and thinks the animals are taking revenge on the hunters. I loved it. Most people I've lent it to hated it.
A: Animals taking revenge. Okay. That's more interesting than I thought.
B: It is. There was a film of it as well, but I haven't seen it.
A: I watch Polish films sometimes. When something comes up. Mostly with my wife we watch crime on Netflix.
B: Which ones?
A: Er, all of them. Is all the same, a detective and he is sad.
B: Ha. That's quite a good review, actually. Pretty much sums up the genre.
A: Yeah. Every one, the detective has problem with his wife.
B: And it's always raining.
A: Always raining, yeah. Is like here.
B: I mostly walk the dog when it's raining. Out along the river, the fens. It's flat for miles.
A: I go fishing. Carp, at a lake near Alton. Sometimes overnight. Is quiet.
B: Overnight? In a tent?
A: Bivvy, yeah. You sit, you wait. Sometimes nothing for twelve hours.
B: That actually sounds quite nice. Nobody talking at you.
